items.headline: Belichick's Tar Heels get the big one — No. 3 Notre Dame rolls into Chapel Hill
items.body: The most fascinating subplot in college football gets a huge test today. Bill Belichick's North Carolina (2-1) hosts third-ranked, unbeaten Notre Dame (4-0) at noon ET on ESPN. Yes, that Belichick — six Super Bowl rings, now running a college program with Bobby Petrino calling the offense. The Irish are favored by three touchdowns, so it's a tall order, but just seeing the hoodie on a college sideline is a whole thing.
items.say: Did you know Bill Belichick coaches college football now? His North Carolina team hosts undefeated Notre Dame today — still so weird seeing him on a college sideline after all those Patriots years. You catch any college ball on Saturdays?

items.headline: Ohtani's back just in time — Dodgers open the NLDS vs. the Braves
items.body: October baseball hits a new gear today, and the Dodgers get a huge lift: Shohei Ohtani is off the injured list (biceps and knee) and in the lineup for Game 1 of the NLDS against Atlanta at Dodger Stadium. L.A. won 100 games this year and has owned the season series with the Braves, but it's best-of-five now — every pitch matters and one bad night can flip a series.
items.say: Shohei Ohtani just came off the injured list right in time for the Dodgers' playoff opener today — the guy pitches AND hits, it's ridiculous. Baseball's in the fun part now. You got a team still alive, or just here for October?

items.headline: The house that Novak built — Djokovic returns to Beijing, still unbeaten there
items.body: Novak Djokovic is back at the China Open for the first time in 11 years, and it's basically his personal fortress: he has never lost in Beijing, a spotless 29-0 with six titles to his name. At 38 he's still rolling through the draw this week, knocking off the home crowd's Bu Yunchaokete along the way. The final's this weekend — can anyone finally spoil the perfect record?
items.say: Djokovic went back to a tournament in Beijing he hasn't played in over a decade — and he's literally never lost there, like 29 and 0. Wild longevity for a guy pushing 40. You follow tennis at all, or just the big Slams?

items.headline: Football with a breakfast kickoff — Commanders & Colts play in London
items.body: Set the alarm (or don't): the NFL heads across the pond tomorrow as Washington takes on Indianapolis at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, a 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff on NFL Network. Jayden Daniels and Terry McLaurin lead the Commanders against Daniel Jones, Jonathan Taylor and the Colts. Two teams trying to prove last year was a fluke — in front of a very loud London crowd.
items.say: There's an NFL game in LONDON on Sunday morning — like 9:30 a.m. kickoff, perfect excuse for football with your coffee. Commanders and Colts. You ever do the early London games, or strictly an afternoon-couch guy?

links.text: WRTV — Colts face Commanders in London on Oct. 4

items.headline: Anne Hathaway's creepy thriller 'Verity' takes over the box office
items.body: The new psychological thriller 'Verity' opened this weekend and is leading the box office (around $27M). Based on Colleen Hoover's bestseller, it stars Anne Hathaway as a famous author with some very dark secrets, Dakota Johnson as the ghostwriter who stumbles onto them, and Josh Hartnett as the husband caught in the middle. Twisty, unsettling and perfect for spooky season.
items.say: That new Anne Hathaway thriller 'Verity' won the box office this weekend — it's the twisty, creepy one based on the huge Colleen Hoover book. Great spooky-season pick. You read the book, or more of a wait-for-the-movie person?

items.headline: Dakota Johnson's big weekend — she hosts SNL tonight, too
items.body: Dakota Johnson is everywhere this weekend: fresh off 'Verity' hitting theaters, she's hosting 'Saturday Night Live' tonight for the third time, with punk-rock favorites Turnstile as the musical guest. She's always game for the weird sketches, so expect a few that get clipped and passed around all week.
items.say: Dakota Johnson's having a moment — new movie out AND she's hosting SNL tonight, with Turnstile playing. She's always fun on that show. You still watch SNL, or just catch the sketches online the next morning?

items.headline: Spooky season gets scary — Mike Flanagan's 'Carrie' hits Prime Video Tuesday
items.body: Horror maestro Mike Flanagan ('The Haunting of Hill House,' 'Midnight Mass') takes on the Stephen King classic, and all eight episodes of 'Carrie' drop Tuesday, Oct. 7, on Prime Video. Newcomer Summer H. Howell plays the bullied teen with telekinetic powers — now amplified by the cruelty of the social-media age — with Matthew Lillard and Amber Midthunder in the cast. The prom is going to be a problem.
items.say: They turned Stephen King's 'Carrie' into a Mike Flanagan series — all eight episodes drop Tuesday on Prime. Perfect timing for October. You into the spooky stuff this time of year, or does horror just stress you out?

items.headline: The Cenobites are back — 'Hellraiser: Revival' launches Wednesday
items.body: For the horror-game crowd (and anyone who grew up terrified of Pinhead): Clive Barker's 'Hellraiser: Revival' arrives Wednesday, Oct. 8, on PS5, Xbox, PC and Switch 2. It's a brutal first-person survival-horror take on the cult film series, puzzle box and all. A genuinely nasty one to play with the lights off this month.
items.say: There's a new Hellraiser video game out Wednesday — the creepy Pinhead/puzzle-box horror series, now a first-person game. Very on-brand for October. You play any games, or is that more the kids' department these days?

items.headline: Wynonna's first solo album in a decade — 'The Hard Truth' is here
items.body: Country legend Wynonna Judd is back with 'The Hard Truth,' her first solo album in 10 years, out now on ANTI- Records. It's a stripped-back, deeply personal record — the lead single 'Girl Who Could Sing' is a letter to the father she never knew, inspired by a drawer of her newspaper clippings his family found after he passed. Raw, warm and a little wrecking.
items.say: Wynonna Judd just put out her first solo album in ten years — really personal, kind of stripped-down country. The first song's a letter to the dad she never got to know. Hits hard. You have an artist you grew up on that you still go back to?
